Article Title: Strategic Autonomy in motion as India hosts 18th BRICS Summit
Article Text:
This would be the 18th summit of the grouping. (Photo: ANI)

India for BRICS

Key Challenges for India

India will host the annual BRICS summit on September 12-13 at Bharat Mandapam, returning to the venue where it held the G20 summit in 2023. That gathering is remembered for the inclusion of the African Union in G20, marking a major step in efforts to bridge the gap between the Western-led global order and the emerging Global South. At BRICS, India will look to leverage that momentum, working with major emerging economies to demand structural reforms of global governance institutions dominated by the West.This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies – Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa, Ethiopia, UAE, Indonesia, Iran, Egypt and Saudi Arabia – along with 10 other partner countries. Together, BRICS nations account for 49 percent of world population, 40 percent of global GDP and 26 percent of international trade.The last time India hosted an in-person BRICS summit was in 2016 in Goa. This year also marks 2 decades of formalisation of the bloc for cooperation on issues related to global economic and political governance. The theme of India's 2026 chairship is Building for Resilience, Innovation, Cooperation and Sustainability, drawing inspiration from PM Narendra Modi's 'humanity first' and people-centric approach to BRICS.This will also be the first summit to see in-person participation by Russian President Vladimir Putin since the start of the Ukraine war. Chinese President Xi Jinping is also visiting India for the first time in 7 years to participate in the summit.Under its chairship, India has so far held over 350 meetings - 25 at the ministerial level including the foreign ministers and national security advisers’ engagements. The ministerial meetings have so far resulted in key outcomes and initiatives spanning agriculture, health, energy, environment, disaster management and also trade, reaffirming commitment to a fair, inclusive and transparent multilateral trading system with WTO at its core.Despite the political fragmentation and economic imbalances associated with the grouping, BRICS remains important for India for multiple reasons, especially in an increasingly uncertain world. For one, it lends India a platform to practice its strategic autonomy and multi-alignment policy, not allowing any one single bloc to acquire excessive leverage over it. That it can simultaneously expand its strategic and technology ties with the West and also work with Quad for a free and open Indo-Pacific reinforces an independent foreign policy. For India, as external affairs minister S Jaishankar has said, BRICS is an embodiment of a multipolar world. India is not giving up on its Western partnerships, only hedging against uncertainty whether from US unpredictability or Chinese ascendancy.BRICS also allows India to showcase its Global South leadership credentials, as it works with other major emerging markets to push for reforms of global institutions like the UNSC, IMF and World Bank that are not representative of the developing world. Support for UNSC reforms is important, although it still falls short of an explicit endorsement of India's permanent membership bid, mainly because of China's presence.India's approach to BRICS is also guided by its complex ties with China. Turning away would mean allowing China to single-handedly shape the agenda of the developing world. BRICS is consensus driven and even for Washington and other Western capitals, India's moderating influence should be of significance as it prevents the bloc from turning into an anti-West platform.There's focus as well on expanding financial architecture as no government would like its trade to be held hostage by instruments it can't control. As Jaishankar has underlined, institutions such as the New Development Bank and the Contingent Reserve Arrangement demonstrate the group's ability to create credible alternatives. For India, these are not initiatives targeted at any currency. In any case, India has officially said it's against de-dollarisation or any attempt to target the US currency. It has also ruled out any proposal for a common BRICS currency.BRICS provides India with markets, along with trade diversification, de-risking and supply-chain opportunities. According to a commerce ministry press release, intra-BRICS merchandise trade reached approximately $1.17 trillion in 2024. India exported an estimated $82 billion in goods to BRICS members in FY2025–26, alongside approximately $31.3 billion in services exports in 2024. BRICS membership deepens India’s trade relationships with Russia (energy), Brazil (agriculture/commodities), Gulf and African countries, diversifying away from overreliance on any single partner.The first of course is to forge a consensus on West Asia that would enable a joint BRICS declaration, a task complicated by the presence of the UAE and Iran in the group. India would not like the event to end with a Chair's Statement, like what happened with the foreign ministers' meeting, knowing well that no BRICS summit has concluded without a comprehensive joint declaration. Foreign secretary Vikram Misri said last week India has received cooperation from all members and the government is working to arrive eventually at a constructive outcome that benefits all BRICS stakeholders. India will focus on drafting a resolution rooted in the UN Charter, dialogue and diplomacy, freedom of navigation and civilian protection, while looking to ringfence economic agreements from contentious political issues by acknowledging respective national positions.Balancing relations with the US is another key concern for India, which is hosting the summit fresh off a tariff firestorm with Washington. US President Donald Trump sees the grouping itself as an assault on the US currency and has threatened to impose 100 percent tariffs on BRICS nations if they work to replace the US dollar. India backs legitimate local-currency settlement, while maintaining it is against any common BRICS currency or China-centered replacement mechanism. As it walks the diplomatic tightrope, India must steer initiatives like the integration of central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) but without appearing to endorse any anti-dollar bloc.Another challenge for India is to prevent China's predominance without destabilising its bilateral relations with Beijing. For all the talk about BRICS' combined power, China enjoys a vastly asymmetrical influence with its trade, investment, manufacturing and critical mineral leverage. Wary of China's efforts to advance its own economic interests, India has not endorsed SCO’s 2030 economic roadmap and it must find a way to work with China in BRICS on shared objectives but without allowing the forum to be co-opted as a Chinese economic or geopolitical platform.This also intersects with the challenge of ensuring that an expanded grouping remains governable and cohesive, especially with countries like Pakistan and Bangladesh pursuing membership with support from Beijing. True multipolarity and consensus-driven equality within the organisation are key imperatives for India.As Jaishankar said while announcing India's summit agenda, BRICS must transition now from a forum for discussions to a platform for delivery. In that spirit, India seems focused on delivering an outcome-oriented summit with key deliverables like a unanimous BRICS declaration, logistics supply-chain cooperation framework, incubator/ startup network, development finance, cross-border payment and continued support for Indian priorities like UNSC reforms and counterterrorism.The inclusion of the African Union was not the only major takeaway from the G20 summit in 2023. Perhaps more dramatic was the last-minute consensus on Ukraine through a compromise language crafted by India, allowing a G20 declaration. India can take confidence from that diplomatic triumph, heading into another tough but potentially rewarding global summit.
Article Summary: India will host the annual brics summit on september 12-13 at bharat mandapam. The theme of india's 2026 chairship is building for resilience, innovation, cooperation and sustainability. This would be the 18th summit of the grouping that brings together 11 major emerging and developing economies.

Article Title: Punjab minister Arora meets UAEIIC secretary general, pitches state as next investment hotspot for UAE capital
Article Text:
Punjab Minister Arora meets UAEIIC Secretary General, pitches state as next investment hotspot for UAE capital. (Photo: ANI)

CHANDIGARH: In a major outreach to attract global capital and boost industrial development as envisioned by Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab Industries and Commerce Minister Aman Arora on Monday met Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi, Secretary General of the UAE International Investment Council (UAEIIC), on the sidelines of the Annual Investment Meeting (AIM) in Dubai to discuss expansive opportunities for mobilising investments into the state.According to the Information and Public Relations Department, Punjab, during the meeting, the Industries Minister discussed Punjab’s vast economic potential with Abdulla Ahmed Al Suwaidi and invited UAE investors to tap into high-growth sectors through government, semi-government and private sector partnerships.Reiterating the state government’s resolve, Arora assured the UAEIIC of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the Punjab Government for global enterprises seeking to set up or expand operations in the state. He emphasised that under the visionary leadership of Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, Punjab is keen to build long-term, mutually beneficial partnerships with UAE-based investors and institutional funds.Highlighting the state’s investor-centric reforms, the Minister underscored the ease of doing business facilitated through ‘Invest Punjab’—the state’s unified single-window platform that delivers prompt statutory approvals and clearances to ensure a smooth, hassle-free investment journey.“Punjab offers a highly conducive entrepreneurial ecosystem, excellent multimodal connectivity, skilled technical manpower, and a transparent governance framework. We invite UAE business leaders to become active partners in Punjab’s transformative economic growth story,” Arora said.The UAE UAEIIC, which unites the UAE’s public and private entities to channel outward foreign direct investment (FDI), welcomed the state delegation's proactive outreach. The engagement focused on establishing robust institutional linkages to enable direct capital inflows and joint ventures between the UAE and Punjab, the Public Relations Department said.Expressing confidence in the discussions, Arora noted that this engagement marks a significant milestone that will pave the way for deeper bilateral economic cooperation, stronger business ties and substantial investment pipelines in Punjab.
Article Summary: Punjab industries and commerce minister aman arora met abdulla ahmed al suwaidi, secretary general of the uae international investment council (uaeiic) the two discussed expansive opportunities for mobilising investments into the state. Arora assured the uaeiic of complete administrative support, handholding and logistical facilitation from the punjab government.

Article Title: Detained Pakistan national repatriated via international border
Article Text:
Detained Pak national repatriated via intl border

JAMMU: A Pakistani man detained near the international border in Jammu’s Kanachak sector last week was repatriated on Monday.Troops of BSF’s 44Bn caught the intruder on Sept 3 near a forward area border outpost. During questioning, he identified himself as Nazir Sadhir from Luni Pundra village in Sialkot and allegedly told investigators that he had inadvertently crossed into Indian territory, officials said.Security agencies investigated his claims, following which BSF officials contacted their Pakistani counterparts and initiated the repatriation process. On Monday, Sadhir was handed over to Pakistan Rangers at Golpattan border outpost along the international border after a flag meeting, officials said.
Article Summary: Detained pak national repatriated via intl border in jammu's kanachak sector. Nazir sadhir from luni pundra village in sialkot allegedly told investigators that he had inadvertently crossed into indian territory. He was handed over to pakistan rangers at golpattan border outpost.

Article Title: Resolution doesn't endorse any specific map: MEA
Article Text:

India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names."India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation. We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.The resolution noted that the Mercator projection remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.It expressed concern that this distortion contributed to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.
Article Summary: India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of un general assembly's sept 4 resolution. The resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.

Article Title: Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet
Article Text:
Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: Lancet

NEW DELHI: Deaths linked to second-hand smoke in India have soared, surging almost 50% since 1990 and claiming 325,600 lives in 2023 alone. According to a study published in The Lancet Public Health Monday, India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after China, with 444 million Indians affected.While India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades, the absolute number of people exposed rose from 375 million in 1990 to 444 million in 2023, an increase of 18.4%. The health toll also rose sharply, with deaths attributable to second-hand smoke climbing from 217,700 to 325,600 during the same period.Fatalities among women rose from 113,400 to 156,900, while deaths among men from 104,300 to 168,700 over the same period. Second-hand smoke also accounted for 9.28 million disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) in India in 2023, representing healthy years lost to premature death, illness or disability.Dr G C Khilnani, chairperson of pulmonary, critical care at PSRI Hospital, said, "Second-hand smoke contributes not only to illness and disability but also to premature deaths and loss of healthy years. Kids and women are particularly vulnerable, with children's developing lungs making them more susceptible to respiratory issues.Smoking should be done outdoors, and greater public awareness is needed."The study links second-hand smoke to ischaemic heart disease, stroke, lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, breast cancer, type 2 diabetes, asthma and lower respiratory infections. Among children, lower respiratory infections were the leading contributor to the disease burden.Globally, 2.71 billion people were exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, contributing to 1.66 million deaths and 44.8 million DALYs. China, India and Indonesia accounted for nearly half of world's exposed population, with China recording 664 million exposed people.
Article Summary: Passive smoking deaths up 50% since 1990: lancet public health study. India had the world's second-highest number of people exposed to second-hand smoke in 2023, after china. India's age-standardised exposure prevalence declined from 43.2% to 30.6% over the last three decades.

Article Title: Karan Rajendra Darda elected INS president for 2026-27
Article Text:
Karan Rajendra Darda of Lokmat has been appointed president of The Indian Newspaper Society for the 2026-27 term, succeeding Vivek Gupta.

NEW DELHI: Karan Rajendra Darda of Lokmat was elected president of The Indian Newspaper Society (INS) for 2026-27 at the organisation’s 87th annual general meeting held in New Delhi on Monday.The INS, the apex body of publishers of newspapers, magazines and periodicals in the country, said Darda succeeds Vivek Gupta of Sanmarg as president.Darda, executive director of Lokmat Media Group, said he would work towards protecting press freedom, strengthening the newspaper industry, encouraging innovation and ensuring that all members, irrespective of their size, have an equal voice.“Together, we will make Indian journalism stronger and future-ready,” Darda said.Darda joined the family business in 2005 and has contributed to the growth, transformation and diversification of Lokmat Media Group, with a focus on innovation, technology, operational efficiency and new business opportunities. He has also championed Project Butterfly, aimed at paperless workflows, and Project Sky, focused on automation and organisational efficiency.MBA from New York and an alumnus of Harvard Business School’s Owner/President Management programme, Darda is also involved in education, sports and community development.He has completed multiple IRONMAN 70.3 races and a full marathon.Tanmay Maheshwari of Amar Ujala was elected deputy president, while Harsha Mathew of Vanitha was elected vice president and Anant Nath of Grihshobhika honorary treasurer for 2026-27.Mary Paul will continue as the secretary general of the society.
Article Summary: Karan rajendra darda of lokmat has been appointed president of the indian newspaper society for the 2026-27 term. He succeeds vivek gupta of sanmarg as president. The ins is the apex body of publishers of newspapers, magazines and periodicals in the country.

Article Title: Malaysia Airlines flight, with 186 passengers onboard, diverts to Chennai after engine snag
Article Text:
Malaysia Airlines' MH156 diverted to Chennai due to issue involving Engine No 2.

Emergency teams put on standby

Air India Express flight also diverted

NEW DELHI: A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai on Monday after a technical issue involving one of its engines, with a full emergency declared at the airport before the aircraft landed safely.Malaysia Airlines flight MH 156 was carrying 186 people when it was diverted. The aircraft landed safely and the airport activated the necessary emergency response arrangements.The technical problem involved "Engine No.2", an airport official said."Further assessment of the aircraft and the technical issue is being carried out by the airline and relevant technical teams," the spokesperson said, adding operations are normal.The aircraft was later moved to a parking bay using a tow vehicle, while the passengers were provided accommodation at the airport.Following the diversion, the relevant airport operational and emergency agencies were alerted and arrangements were made to handle the aircraft's arrival safely.The aircraft landed without any untoward incident. The airline's technical teams are now assessing the reported engine issue.Airport operations continued normally after the aircraft was brought to the parking area.Separately, an Air India Express flight from Tiruchirappalli to Singapore was also diverted to Chennai on Monday following a technical issue.A "local standby was declared" at Chennai airport and emergency response arrangements were kept ready.The aircraft landed safely and vacated the runway on its own power. The airline's engineering and technical team is assessing the issue."All operations are normal," the official added.
Article Summary: Malaysia airlines' mh156 diverted to chennai due to issue involving engine no 2. Emergency teams put on standby before aircraft landed safely. Air india express flight also diverted following a technical issue. The aircraft was later moved to a parking bay using a tow vehicle.

Article Title: Far-right AfD makes historic breakthrough in Germany, wins 44% in state poll
Article Text:
Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised for a historic breakthrough in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt.

Germany’s far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is poised for a historic breakthrough in the eastern state of Saxony-Anhalt, opening the prospect of the party seeking to govern despite falling short of an outright majority.With most interim results counted, the AfD was projected to secure a record 44% of the vote and far ahead of the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which stood at 17%.Ulrich Siegmund, the AfD’s prominent leader in Saxony-Anhalt, described the result as “sensational” and said the party wanted to begin governing as soon as possible.According to the BBC report, a victory would mark an unprecedented development in post-war Germany, where no far-right party has previously taken control of a state government. State-level power would give the AfD influence over areas including policing, education and culture.Saxony-Anhalt, home to about 2.1 million people, has been a particular focus of concern because the state’s AfD branch is classified as “right-wing extremist” by Germany’s domestic intelligence service. Siegmund, 35, rejects the designation.Siegmund and the party’s national co-leaders, Alice Weidel and Tino Chrupalla, celebrated as exit polls showed the AfD was on course to more than double its 2021 vote share.The AfD’s strong performance was quickly described by political opponents and commentators as a major turning point, highlighting the growing influence of the far-right party in German politics. Public broadcaster Das Erste even replaced its long-running crime drama Tatort with special coverage examining the significance of the result.“This isn’t just about Saxony-Anhalt,” Siegmund told supporters. “It’s a signal for the whole of Germany - a self-confident signal.”Commentators and political opponents spoke of the outcome as a watershed and break with the past. Main TV channel Das Erste cancelled its legendary crime drama Tatort to focus on what the result meant.“This result is not just about Saxony-Anhalt,” Siegmund told supporters, calling it “a signal for the whole of Germany — a confident signal.”The result also drew attention abroad. US President Donald Trump shared a screenshot of the German election projection on his Truth Social platform, which Russian presidential envoy Kirill Dmitriev later reposted, describing the outcome as a “historic win for the pragmatic AfD”.Dmitriev had previously praised the Russia-friendly party as one offering “hope and reason” and greater cooperation for Germany. US Vice-President JD Vance also backed the AfD ahead of Germany’s federal election last year, a move that drew criticism in Germany over alleged foreign political interference.Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk, however, offered a sharply contrasting reaction. The centre-right leader said that in Poland, “only idiots and traitors can rejoice at the triumph of the AfD.”Despite its strong performance, the AfD lacks the seats needed to govern alone, leaving Ulrich Siegmund facing a difficult path to power. He has so far ruled out leading a minority government, even as the party’s national leadership considers that option possible.Siegmund said the AfD would instead be willing to seek support from individual lawmakers or another party. “If necessary there’ll just be new elections, then we’d just get 50 or 55%,” he said.The outcome was also closely tied to the performance of the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), whose ability to clear the 5% threshold needed to enter the state parliament remained uncertain for several hours. Interim results eventually showed the party had crossed the threshold, meaning the AfD would not gain the additional seats it might otherwise have secured.The AfD was projected to win 39 of the 83 seats in Saxony-Anhalt’s state parliament, leaving it three seats short of the 42 required for an outright majority.
Article Summary: Afd poised for historic breakthrough in eastern state of saxony-anhalt. Party projected to secure a record 44% of the vote and far ahead of cdu. No far-right party has previously taken control of a state government in germany.

Article Title: Eiffel Tower shuts after female staff allegedly sidelined during Hindu group's visit
Article Text: NEW DELHI: The Eiffel Tower was closed to visitors on Monday after staff staged a walkout over allegations that female employees were moved away from their workstations during a visit by a Hindu religious group linked to the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS), as reported by Euronews.The iconic Paris landmark's operator, SETE, said the closure was due to "exceptional circumstances".The protest followed a visit by around 100 people linked to the BAPS Hindu movement, which inaugurated a new temple in France over the weekend.Diane Davoine, a union representative, told French TV that female workers had been "moved away from their workstations as the delegation passed by" during the group's visit on Saturday.Eiffel Tower employees condemned what they described as "professional instructions that led to female employees being sidelined, replaced and made invisible because of their sex."SETE acknowledged that the Hindu delegation had requested that the visit be organised to limit "interactions with women", but said "these conditions should not have been accepted."In a statement on Monday evening, the BAPS Hindu temple in Paris said it took the concerns "very seriously" and apologised for "any pain or inconvenience caused.""Due to the size of our delegation, the visit was arranged in conjunction with the Eiffel Tower team at the start of normal opening hours to avoid disrupting or inconveniencing others," it said."To the best of our knowledge, at no point was anyone prevented access to the Eiffel Tower," it continued, adding that it believed in the "universal values of mutual respect and service."Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire said on X that he was "aware of the outcry among the employees of the Eiffel Tower" and called it "unacceptable" that such conditions were agreed to."These are not my values, nor are they the values that the Eiffel Tower should uphold, where everyone must be able to move about and act freely, without distinction between women and men," he wrote, adding that an investigation into the incident would be launched.National assembly president Yael Braun-Pivet also condemned the incident."I refuse to accept that women should be told to step aside to meet the demands of foreign visitors," she said. "Welcoming others never means giving up our values. In France, women are fully present in public life. No one tells them to become invisible there."The incident comes day after the Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) inaugurated its first major Hindu temple in France, marking a significant moment for the Hindu community in the country.Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India-France ties while addressing the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris. He said the strategic partnership between the two countries was particularly special as it was built on a foundation of long-standing cultural and political ties.The PM said he hoped the grand temple would stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity between India and France.“In recent years, relations between India and France have reached new heights. Together with my friend, President (Emmanuel) Macron, both nations are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership,” he said.
Article Summary: The iconic paris landmark's operator, sete, said the closure was due to "exceptional circumstances" the protest followed a visit by around 100 people linked to the baps hindu movement. A union representative said female workers had been "moved away from their workstations as the delegation passed by"

Article Title: ‘Russia ready to negotiate’: Zelenskyy after meeting US envoys Witkoff and Kushner
Article Text:
Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy

(With AP inputs)

Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Monday (local time) said US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff told him that Russia is “ready to negotiate” when they met him in Kyiv after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.“Russia really thinks that this winter can help them break us. But the Trump administration could pressure Putin to de-escalate... Putin doesn’t want to upset President Trump,” Zelenskyy told US news outlet Axios.“The US envoys told me that the Russians are ready to negotiate,” he added.Elaborating on his discussions with Witkoff and Kushner, the Ukrainian leader noted that the weekend talks included US proposals concerning energy facilities, grain shipments, and oil and gas exports, but declined to provide further details.“The US is seeking to restart negotiations between Ukraine and Russia and wants to ensure the coming winter is different from previous ones. The aim is to make progress before or during winter to ‘bring (the) sides closer to peace,’” Zelenskyy said.Russia has targeted Ukraine’s energy infrastructure every winter since the war began in February 2022, leaving millions without electricity and heating as temperatures have fallen as low as -20°C.The visits to Moscow and Kyiv by Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner mark Washington’s latest effort to break the diplomatic deadlock in Europe’s deadliest conflict since World War II.US President Donald Trump had repeatedly claimed during his campaign that, if elected, he would end the Russia-Ukraine conflict “in 24 hours.” Last August, more than six months into his second and final term, Trump hosted Putin in Alaska to discuss the conflict, marking their first meeting since Trump returned to office. However, the meeting ended without any significant breakthrough.
Article Summary: Ukraine president volodymyr zelenskyy said us envoys jared kushner and steve witkoff told him that russia is ‘ready to negotiate’ zelenskiy said the talks included us proposals concerning energy facilities, grain shipments, and oil and gas exports.

Article Title: Yemen conflict widens: Houthis claim strikes on Saudi airport, air base and Aramco sites
Article Text:
Drones and ballistic missiles at King Khalid Air Base in Khamis Mushait and Abha International Airport in southern Saudi Arabia. (GIF: @theinformant_x)

Houthi attacks follow September 7 escalation

Houthi official puts prison toll at 11

Fighting intensifies near Bab al-Mandab

Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis said on September 8 that they had launched missiles and drones at Abha International Airport, King Khalid air base and Aramco facilities in Abha and Jizan.“Yemeni drones and missiles pound the Saudi enemy,” Houthi media outlet Ansarollah said on Telegram. Another Ansarollah post named the airport, military base and oil facilities among the targets.The Saudi-led coalition said on September 7 that 73 people were injured in Houthi attacks on civilian and economic sites. The attacks affected Abha, Khamis Mushait, Najran and Jazan, and the coalition said it would respond firmly, according to Reuters.On the same day, the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of air strikes and cruise missile attacks in Jawf, Al-Bayda, Marib and Taiz. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said the alleged Saudi attacks “will not go unanswered or unpunished”. Saudi Arabia did not publicly confirm the Houthi allegations.One of the alleged Saudi strikes hit a prison in Al-Hazm, Jawf province, according to Houthi media. The Houthi-run health ministry initially reported seven deaths, including a child, and at least seven injuries, according to the Associated Press.Separately, Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said their own warplanes struck Houthi positions on September 7.By September 8, Jawf civil defence chief Hassan Saboula put the Houthi-reported prison death toll at 11 and said 20 inmates remained missing beneath the rubble, according to the Houthi-run Al-Masirah. Houthi-affiliated Saba said a child visiting the facility was among those killed.The latest exchange comes amid fighting near Yemen’s Red Sea coast. More than 300 people have been killed in the recent clashes, while hundreds of families have been forced from their homes. The Houthis are pressing an offensive for territory along the Bab al-Mandab Strait.Bab al-Mandab connects the Gulf of Aden with the Red Sea, which leads north to the Suez Canal. The route has gained importance for Saudi crude shipments as Iran’s blockade restricts traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
Article Summary: Yemen’s iran-backed houthis said they had launched missiles and drones at abha international airport, king khalid air base and aramco facilities in abha and jizan. The saudi-led coalition said on september 7 that 73 people were injured in houthi attacks on civilian and economic sites.

Article Title: PLA report warns Chinese cities of potential nuclear attacks, flags Japan as ‘threat’
Article Text:
AI-generated image

Why report singled out Japan

What a potential nuclear attack on a Chinese city look like

A new study by China’s People’s Liberation Army (PLA) Rocket Force has warned Chinese cities to prepare for potential nuclear attacks, singling out Japan as a “major danger signal” to the world.According to the report, the likelihood of a large-scale global nuclear war was “relatively low,” South China Morning Post reported.“However, the possibility cannot be ruled out that small or medium-sized nuclear-armed or potentially nuclear-armed states, driven by geopolitical or religious conflicts, could carry out a single nuclear-weapon terrorist attack on neighbouring countries or on key cities of major powers,” it said.The study noted that Tokyo had yet to join the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, the first legally binding international agreement banning nuclear arms, adopted in 2017. It also claimed Japan was considering changes to its long-standing “three non-nuclear principles” of not possessing, producing or permitting the introduction of nuclear weapons.“Japan has still not acceded to the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, and the current Japanese government is even openly considering revising the principle of ‘non-introduction of nuclear weapons’ within its ‘three non-nuclear principles’, sending a major danger signal to the international community,” the report stated.In January 2022, the United Nations P5 — China, the United States, Russia, Britain, and France — the five permanent members of the UN Security Council — issued a joint statement affirming that “a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought”.But the PLA study warned: “Once certain countries or terrorist groups take such a risk, the possibility that Chinese cities could suffer a nuclear terrorist attack cannot be ruled out.”An official Chinese report released in January alleged that Tokyo “may already have produced weapons-grade plutonium in secret” and possessed “the technological and economic capabilities to achieve nuclear armament in a short period of time.”The January report also claimed Japan had “established a comprehensive nuclear fuel cycle system and possesses robust nuclear industrial capabilities”.The PLA Rocket Force study also modelled a scenario in which a major Chinese city was hit by a single, low-yield nuclear terrorist attack involving a tactical weapon.Drawing on historical data from the 1945 Hiroshima bombing in Japan, along with simulations conducted worldwide, the researchers identified a range of challenges for medical teams, including hazardous conditions, widespread social disorder and complex patterns of injuries.Beijing has already established an emergency rescue network with more than 30 bases to treat casualties from a nuclear attack. The researchers called for further expansion of treatment capacity, additional resources and specialised training.They also recommended that local authorities stockpile emergency supplies, including antibiotics and radiation-protection equipment, and keep them in a state of “combat readiness”.Public education should also be strengthened on nuclear and radiation safety, rescue protocols and protective measures to minimise panic and irrational behaviour during an emergency.Compared with the medical response to an accident at a civilian nuclear facility, even a low-yield nuclear terrorist attack could result in heavy casualties and complex, multi-trauma injuries.Such an event would pose a “huge test” for the medical capacity of any city or country, the authors wrote, urging China to “prepare for a rainy day”.Beijing has repeatedly accused Tokyo of pursuing “remilitarisation” and has long voiced suspicions about its nuclear ambitions.
Article Summary: China's people's liberation army rocket force warned chinese cities to prepare for potential nuclear attacks. Study singled out japan as a “major danger signal’ to the world. Tokyo has yet to join the treaty on the prohibition of nuclear weapons.

Article Title: 'Strike our assets & you get struck': Iran threatens US energy assets in Gulf after latest clashes
Article Text:
Iran threatens US oil, gas assets.

Iran tightens restrictions

Oil flows disrupted

Iran has threatened to retaliate against any new US attacks on its assets, warning that American oil and gas interests and energy infrastructure across the Gulf could be targeted as tensions escalate over the Strait of Hormuz."Strike our assets and you get struck," Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said after US and Iranian forces traded strikes on shipping over the weekend, pushing oil prices to near six-week highs on Monday, according to Reuters.The warning came amid growing concerns that the conflict could escalate further, with diplomatic efforts showing little progress towards restoring normal energy flows through the Gulf.Iran has tightened restrictions on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global oil and gas supplies, since the war began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28.On Sunday, senior Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei said Tehran would soon announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf and establish a new shipping corridor through the strait.Rezaei said the restricted zone would begin where a US naval blockade of Iran starts and extend into parts of the Gulf.Ships entering the area would be placed on an Iranian sanctions list."We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran," Rezaei said.Qalibaf later reinforced the warning in an apparent response to US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who had described Iran's oil tanker fleet as "defenceless"."It's simple: the oil and gas production chain here is sprawling, accessible, and exposed. American oil and gas companies across these waters and facilities share that exposure," Qalibaf, who is Iran's top negotiator, wrote on X.Tensions have intensified after a relative lull through much of August and the collapse of an interim ceasefire reached in June.Earlier on Saturday, US forces struck three Iranian oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island, Iran's main oil export hub, according to US Central Command. The strikes followed attacks by Iran's Revolutionary Guards on US warships operating in the region.Shipping data showed that an average of only 10 commodity vessels a day passed through the Strait of Hormuz over the past 10 days, the lowest level since May. The strait is a critical energy chokepoint. Before the war, it carried about one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas shipments.Regional tensions were also heightened by Israeli strikes on a town in southern Lebanon that killed at least 12 people on Monday, according to Lebanon's health ministry.The strikes have raised fears of a renewed Israeli military campaign despite a June ceasefire with Iran-backed Hezbollah. Tehran has insisted that any lasting agreement with Washington must include an end to Israeli attacks in Lebanon.Iran has said it will step up efforts to address problems caused by US sanctions, which have put further pressure on its economy.Three senior Iranian sources told Reuters that Washington's campaign to restrict Iranian oil exports and curb sanctions evasion is becoming increasingly difficult for Tehran to withstand.Qalibaf acknowledged over the weekend that Iran's challenges extend beyond the battlefield. Alongside the military conflict, he cited inflation, unemployment, currency volatility and market instability as major domestic problems.The conflict has also affected Gulf oil producers, including the United Arab Emirates, which has faced Iranian missile attacks and attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz.The disruption is also being felt in the United States, where higher fuel prices have added to economic pressures and could weigh on President Donald Trump's popularity ahead of November's midterm elections.
Article Summary: Iran threatens us oil, gas assets. Iran tightens restrictions on shipping through the strait of hormuz. Oil flows disrupted, pushing oil prices to near six-week highs. Iranian parliament speaker mohammad baqer qalibaf: "strike our assets and you get struck"

Article Title: Iran to announce new restricted zone in Gulf in the coming days
Article Text:
Iran to announce new restricted zone in Gulf in the coming days

Dubai:

Iran said it will announce a new restricted zone in the Gulf in the coming days, along with maps of a new shipping corridor through the Strait of Hormuz, as a weekend exchange of strikes on shipping sent oil prices higher on Monday. The new restricted zone will begin from where the US blockade of Iran begins and extend into areas of the Gulf, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council, said on Sunday in an interview with state TV.Few details were provided on the plan, but Rezaei said any ship entering the new zone would be added to a sanctions list.In addition, maps detailing passage routes for the Strait of Hormuz, a vital energy conduit largely closed to tanker traffic, would also be approved soon, Rezaei said. “The maps of a new international corridor which lies in Iranian and Omani waters and in which Iran will have management have been agreed and should be signed in the coming days,” he said.“We will only commit to the Strait of Hormuz being open when they (the Americans) stop the sabotage, threats and attacks on Iran,” Rezaei added.Iran govt to raise fuel price for heavy users: Iran will raise the price of gasoline for users surpassing 110 litres per month starting Tuesday, a govt spokesperson said Sunday.The price of the first and second quotas, which include 110 litres, will remain unchanged, but the price of the third quota will be raised to 100,000 Iranian rials per litre (around 4 US cents based on the free-market rate), Fatemeh Mohajerani said in comments carried by state media. The increase in Iran’s gasoline price, which is one of the lowest in the world, was discussed by the govt and postponed amid concerns it could trigger new protests. Iran experienced widespread protests in 2019 over the same issue. The higher fuel price will only affect consumers who require more than 110 litres per month, Mohajerani said.
Article Summary: Iran to announce new restricted zone in gulf in the coming days. New restricted zone will begin from where the us blockade of iran begins and extend into areas of the gulf. Maps detailing passage routes for the strait of hormuz, a vital energy conduit, would also be approved soon.

Article Title: Indonesia air travel resumes after two-day disruption from volcanic ash
Article Text:
Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday.

Air travel across Indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early Tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from Anak Krakatau, which disrupted nearly 3,000 flights.Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and Halim Perdanakusuma Airport in Jakarta, along with Husein Sastranegara Airport in West Java’s Bandung and two smaller airports in Banten province, reopened shortly after midnight, Transportation Minister Dudy Purwagandhi said.Three other airports, including Radin Inten II Airport in Lampung at the southern end of Sumatra, remained closed until 10 a.m. despite improving conditions. Atung Bungsu Airport in Pagar Alam, South Sumatra, resumed normal operations on Monday morning.“We are taking a cautious approach because wind direction can change rapidly,” Purwagandhi said in a statement. “We want to make sure volcanic ash has moved away from airports around Anak Krakatau.”While tests at several airports found no traces of volcanic ash, the prolonged closures would provide additional time to inspect and clean runways, taxiways, aircraft and other equipment that may have been exposed to the ash, Purwagandhi said.The continuous eruption at Anak Krakatau, marked by lava fountains and loud explosions, subsided on Sunday, but the volcanic island remained active on Tuesday morning. Eruptions were recorded at 5:08 a.m. and 5:34 a.m., although the height of the ash column could not be determined.A massive two-day air travel disruption affected approximately 341,000 passengers as airport closures on Sunday and Monday grounded nearly 2,961 flights—including 622 international routes—according to reports by the Associated Press.The government also allowed schools in areas affected by volcanic ash to temporarily switch to online classes to limit students’ exposure to the ash.Anak Krakatau is a volcanic island in the Sunda Strait, located between Indonesia’s main islands of Java and Sumatra. Its name means “child of Krakatau” and refers to the volcano that emerged from the remnants of the infamous Krakatau, whose massive 1883 eruption triggered a period of global cooling.In 2018, an eruption of Anak Krakatau generated a tsunami that killed at least 430 people across Sumatra and Java. Researchers believe the volcanic activity triggered an underwater landslide, causing part of the volcano’s southwestern slope to collapse and displace a large volume of seawater.The volcano has remained at Indonesia’s second-highest alert level since July, with authorities urging residents, tourists and fishermen to stay at least 3 kilometres (1.9 miles) away from the active crater.
Article Summary: Air travel across indonesia’s capital region began returning to normal early tuesday following a two-day shutdown triggered by volcanic ash from anak krakatau. Soekarno-hatta international airport and halim perdanakusuma airport in jakarta reopened shortly after midnight.

Article Title: Ollie Millroy crash: Wife says ‘can’t believe he’s alive’ as Loek Hartog hailed ‘superhero’ after China GT fireball
Article Text:
Ollie Millroy crash: Wife says ‘can’t believe he’s alive’ as Loek Hartog hailed ‘superhero’ after China GT fireball

Ollie Millroy’s wife Fern gives update after Shanghai crash

Loek Hartog explains why he stopped for Ollie Millroy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

British racing driver Ollie Millroy is recovering in a Shanghai hospital after surviving a huge crash that left his Ferrari engulfed in flames during a China GT race. Millroy, 36, suffered broken ribs, a broken collarbone, a broken hand and finger, and a bruised lung. His wife, Fern Millroy, said she still cannot believe he survived and credited Dutch driver Loek Hartog with saving his life. Hartog, 23, stopped his own Porsche, ran to the burning Ferrari and pulled Millroy out. Millroy later said he owes his life to the rival who risked his own safety to help him.Fern said Millroy underwent surgery and was being closely watched at the hospital. She wrote: “Surgery went well yesterday. It took several hours, main work being his right hand. He now has metal along the entirety of his clavicle right side, metal inside his right hand, six broken ribs supported with a compression wrap and on high flow oxygen whilst his lung recovers.”She added that doctors tried to take him off oxygen, but his oxygen level was too low. Fern also thanked the hospital staff and said more X-rays and a CT scan were planned.“I still can’t believe he’s alive, purely down to our real life superhero Loek Hartog,” she wrote.The crash happened during the China GT race at Shanghai International Circuit on Saturday. Millroy’s Ferrari was hit during a multi-car accident and quickly caught fire. Video from Hartog’s car shows the Dutchman stopping and running towards the wreck.Hartog first tried to reach Millroy from the driver’s side. He then used a fire extinguisher to fight the flames before pulling Millroy from the other side of the Ferrari. Motorsport.com reported that the rescue took about 49 seconds from the time Hartog left his car.Millroy later thanked Hartog from his hospital bed, saying: “I am still alive tonight, entirely thanks to one man. Loek Hartog stopped instantly with no flag marshals or fire crews in sight, and risked his own life to get me out of the car.”He added: “I don’t remember anything between 30 seconds before the crash and 1 hour after it, but I will remember his incredible act of bravery for the rest of my life.”Hartog said he did not think twice after seeing the Ferrari turn into a fireball.“When I saw a car turning into a huge fireball far ahead, there wasn’t really a decision to make,” he wrote. “From what I had seen, I genuinely believed the driver might not be able to get out by himself. I stopped, got out and went towards the car. There was never a moment of doubt.”He also admitted the rescue was frightening, saying there were moments when he did not know if he could get Millroy out. Still, Hartog said the focus should not be on him and that many people in the same situation would have reacted similarly.Millroy remains in hospital in Shanghai. His condition has been described as stable, while his recovery continues after the serious injuries suffered in the crash.
Article Summary: British racing driver ollie millroy is recovering in a shanghai hospital after surviving a huge crash that left his ferrari engulfed in flames during a china gt race. His wife, fern millroy, said she still cannot believe he survived and credited dutch driver loek hartog with saving his life.

Article Title: Kanpur engineer detained in Moscow; embassy seeks consular access
Article Text:
An Indian engineer working in Moscow was reportedly detained by Russian police.





LUCKNOW: Soon after a Kanpur-based engineer working in Moscow was reportedly detained by Russian police, prompting his wife to appeal to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath for his release and safe return to India, the Indian Embassy in Russia sought consular access.Chandan Gupta, 40, had travelled to Russia with his family on a work visa and is working with a Noida-based Indian company. His wife, Sneha, has released a video seeking govt intervention, claiming that Russian police took her husband away from their residence late Sunday.Taking note of Sneha’s video, the Indian Embassy posted on X: “We have seen a social media post by an Indian national regarding her husband. We are in touch with her and the local authorities in the matter. As per law enforcement authorities, it is a legal matter and they are looking into it. The Embassy has also sought consular access.”The embassy issued the statement soon after Chandan’s wife expressed fears that he could be pressured into joining the Russian military. “I am afraid that my husband may be sent to the Russian Army forcibly,” she said, appealing to the authorities to ensure his safety.There is no independent confirmation so far that Chandan has been recruited or is being sent to the Russian military.Sneha said she is currently in Moscow with their 10-year-old child and is finding it difficult to understand and navigate the situation as she does not speak Russian.In her video appeal of a little over one minute, Sneha claimed Russian police arrived at around 12.30 am and took Chandan with them. She claimed that she was subsequently informed that her husband had been kept in custody. According to her, Chandan had not committed any act that warranted his detention, and she has not been given adequate information about the circumstances surrounding his arrest.However, reports reaching India said Chandan was detained along with a friend, Ashish, around 11.30 pm (local time) on Sept 5 from Moscow’s Red Square premises on charges of drunkenness and allegedly breaking the glass of a nearby ambulance. “They are currently detained at the Baumanskaya police station in Moscow. The embassy has raised the matter with the local authorities and requested their release. Meanwhile, consular access has also been sought,” sources said.According to her, officials have told her that Chandan would be released, but she said she has not received a concrete update about when or under what circumstances he would be set free.
Article Summary: Chandan gupta, 40, had travelled to russia with his family on a work visa. He is working with a noida-based indian company. His wife, sneha, has released a video seeking govt intervention. The indian embassy in russia has sought consular access.

Elon Musk on use of the word Nazi

Article Title: Republican Mayor of American city on Lake Ontario' shore rejects the name change to 'Lake America' that Google and Apple have adopted; says: My community …
Article Text:
The renaming of ‘Lake Ontario’ and local pushback

A Bipartisan and cross-border backlash

The Republican mayor of Oswego, New York, Robert Corradino, has rejected the renaming of Lake Ontario to “Lake America,” a change enacted by US President Donald Trump through an executive order on August 27. While Google and Apple Maps have already adopted the new name for US users, Corradino said his community is “taking the renaming very personally” and will continue to use Lake Ontario in all signage, tourism materials, and official communications. According to a report by National Post, Corradino emphasized that Lake Ontario is central to Oswego’s identity, citing its economic importance through charter boats, cruise ships, and tourism.Robert Corradino emphasized that Lake Ontario's name is rooted in a Huron Indigenous word meaning "lake of shining waters," predating the province of Ontario itself, which took its name from the lake in 1867. “Lake Ontario is in the DNA of Osweganians. Everything that we are emanates from the lake,” he said. The mayor also noted that Canadian tourism, vital to local businesses, has dropped substantially following the breakdown of US-Canada trade negotiations last month.Statistics Canada data shows Canadian travel to the US fell 10.6% in the first quarter of 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.Corradino reaffirmed Oswego’s stance: “Lake Ontario has carried its name for hundreds of years. It is a name rooted in history, geography, and the shared identity of the communities that surround it. The city of Oswego will continue using the name that reflects our history and honors the generations who have lived, worked, and built their lives along its shores.”Recently, Oswego County legislators from both parties passed a resolution rejecting the renaming, citing rebranding costs for taxpayers and businesses. MapQuest also refused to adopt the "Lake America" name, boosting its app store rankings.Trump's order has drawn criticism well beyond Oswego. Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton responded to the renaming with a brief rebuttal on X, while Vermont Senator Bernie Sanders said the American public has no appetite for calling the lake "Lake America."North of the border, Carney noted on social media that the name Lake Ontario derives from the Wendat word "Ontari'io," meaning the lake is beautiful and big, and that it predates both Canadian Confederation and the U.S. Declaration of Independence by more than 400 years. He argued that acknowledging reality means continuing to call it Lake Ontario. Conservative Party leader Pierre Poilievre echoed the sentiment, saying the lake was never Trump's to rename on a whim.Ontario Premier Doug Ford went a step further on Saturday, unveiling a new "Lake Ontario" sign in Winona, Ontario, declaring in a video posted to X that the lake carried that name long before Trump and would continue to carry it long after he's gone.
Article Summary: The mayor of oswego, new york, has rejected the renaming of lake ontario to “lake america,” a change enacted by us president donald trump through an executive order on august 27. Robert corradino emphasized that lake ontario's name is rooted in a huron indigenous word meaning "lake of shining waters," predating the province of ontario itself, which took its name from it in 1867.
